name: Edo Yumi
materials: Bamboo and wood, lacquered and bound
blurb: Bound in red and black from tip to tip, strung, and taller than the archer who drew it.
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0)

name: Su Yari
blurb: A straight blade on its full lacquered haft, bound in red below the head.
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0)

name: Sindhi Battle Axe
blurb: Steel from edge to butt, engraved with flowers and an elephant. Sind, around 1800.
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0)

name: Kagi Yari
blurb: The blade rests in its sheath. The iron hook below it caught an enemy's shaft.
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0)

name: Swiss Halberd
materials: Steel; new rectangular wood haft with planed corners
blurb: Axe, beak and spike in one Swiss head, mounted on a later haft.
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0)

name: Italian Glaive
materials: Plain steel blade, carved wooden haft with protruding tongue of steel
blurb: A broad blade of the 1400s on a carved wooden haft.
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0)

name: Scandinavian Battle Axe
blurb: A northern war axe of the 1400s, its haft wound with riveted iron.
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0)

name: Seven-Flanged Mace
materials: Gilded russet steel; with chiseled foliate decoration
blurb: Gilded russet steel chiseled with leaves. A horseman's mace, around 1540.
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0)
